items.calibration: measuring the melting point of lead and aluminum
items.crucible: boron nitride layer on these alumina crucibles
items.quote: DTA measurements are performed with a DSC404C (Netzsch). The calibration of the apparatus was checked by measuring the melting point of lead and aluminum. The temperature is in good agreement with the accepted values of the thermodynamic tables [32] with an experimental error of ±1 K. For all the analyses, a heating and cooling rate of 2 K/min was used. Such a value gives a correct compromise between variation of the thermodynamic equilibrium, signal intensity and time. Standard alumina crucibles react with the liquid Mn-Si alloys and after the measurement, crucibles become brown. Spraying a boron nitride layer on these alumina crucibles prevent such reactions.

items.label: Mn-Si alloys
items.quote: The Mn-Si alloys are synthesized from their constitutive elements, Mn (99.8%, from Alfa Aesar) and Si (99.9999%, from Alfa Aesar), by arc melting in a watercooled copper crucible under argon (99.995%). Prior to fusion, the Mn and Si elements are crushed and weighed in different atomic percentages. The samples are then melted three times in order to obtain homogeneous samples.
